The candidate chooses the Schedule D Tax Worksheet through its helper f1040.h_use_sdtw = sdtw.use1250 or sdtw.use28 or f4952.line4g > 0. sdtw.use1250 and sdtw.use28 are flow helpers inside that worksheet ("Compute lines 35-40 when Schedule D line 19 is positive"; "Follow printed flow to lines 41-43", both requiring the worksheet to continue past line 32), not the test for using it: sdtw.use28 holds when Schedule D line 19 is zero, so a filer whose Schedule D lines 18 and 19 are both zero is sent to the Schedule D Tax Worksheet whenever its flow passes line 32. i1040sd p. 15, Schedule D Tax Worksheet: "Complete this worksheet only if line 18 or line 19 of Schedule D is more than zero and lines 15 and 16 of Schedule D are gains or if you file Form 4952 and you have an amount on line 4g ... Otherwise, complete the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet". Whether the tax amount differs is not established (with no 28% or section 1250 gain the two worksheets usually agree), so the error is in the worksheet chosen. Its fallback to qdcg.line25 when neither worksheet applies (the Exception on the same page, "Don't use the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet or this worksheet") equals the Tax Table or Tax Computation Worksheet tax on line 15 (lines 2 to 4 zero, line 25 the smaller of two equal taxes), which is representation. Note: i1040gi p. 36 (the line 16 method list) was not among the pages given; i1040sd p. 15, which was given, decides the line.

Continue ... 3. Are you filing Form 4797 ...? No. STOP You can't take the credit". Witness by reading: a single filer with one qualifying child, $20,000 of wages and $15,000 of taxable interest (investment income over $11,950, no Form 4797): project $0, candidate the Worksheet A line 6 amount for $20,000 of earned income.
